summary: @servicetitan/eslint-config preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated 727 KB payload at install time
details: package.json declares `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"`. setup.mjs is obfuscated (hex-named identifiers, string-array indirection) and, when Bun is not already present, downloads a Bun binary from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temp directory, chmods it executable, and runs it against a sibling file math_init.js via `execFileSync(bunPath, [path.join(D, 'math_init.js')], {stdio:'inherit', cwd:D})`. math_init.js is a ~727 KB heavily obfuscated blob (string-array rotation function `WV8StW`, hex identifiers, dense numeric/string constant table) that is not declared in package.json `files` (declared entries are dist, src, single.js, mono.js, qa.js); setup.mjs is likewise undeclared. An ESLint configuration package has no legitimate need to fetch a second language runtime at install and use it to execute a bundled obfuscated script. The Bun-executed code path bypasses Node-based auditing tooling. On `npm install`, arbitrary attacker-controlled code runs on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
